clue.text: Bold action — being human in irregular retreat?

indicators.note: the human piece sits inside the turned-round word
to retreat is to go backwards, so the word for irregular is read in reverse

parts.note: odd means irregular or strange
'to err is human', so being human is erring

explanation.surface: A question about whether brave deeds are really just a disorderly human retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'to err is human' supplies the middle; 'retreat' looks like the surface's noun but is the signal that turns the word for irregular backwards, and 'in' sets the human piece inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Daring deeds or heroic courage are the classic sense of this old-fashioned hyphenated phrase.

clue.text: Ruin suit

definitions.meaning: to finish off or destroy someone, as in 'that will finish him'
to be adequate or serve someone's needs, as in 'that will serve me well enough'

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to ruin and, informally in British use, to be enough for or satisfy.

clue.text: Clergyman holding a source of power

indicators.note: the clergyman's title grips the article inside it

parts.note: a rector is a parish clergyman

explanation.surface: A vicar clutching an energy supply.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear plant's core apparatus generates energy, making it a power source.

clue.text: Keep yellow tops after wearing black

indicators.note: the picked letters come after the piece for wearing

parts.note: if you are wearing something you are in it

indicators.note: the tops of words are their first letters, taken from the two words before

explanation.surface: Advice to keep the yellow tops on after dressing in black.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tops' takes K and Y from Keep and yellow; 'after' puts them behind IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stained like ink is very dark, so the adjective means black.

clue.text: Dig for food

definitions.meaning: to root about in the soil
informal word for something to eat

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to dig in the ground; as a noun it is slang for something to eat.

clue.text: Making the best of work with insufficient time, I croon

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work

indicators.note: insufficient means falling short, so the word for time loses its last letter

parts.note: the word itself
to croon is to sing softly

explanation.surface: A singer with too little time still making the most of a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To get the most out of something is to make the best use of it.

clue.text: Alexander's troops taking what's inside

parts.note: the SAS is the British Special Air Service regiment

indicators.note: the inside of the word what is its middle letters

explanation.surface: Alexander the Great's army capturing what lies within.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' gives HA from the middle of 'what'.
explanation.definitionFit: This Russian pet name is a diminutive of Alexander, so it is Alexander's familiar form.

clue.text: Playwright giving way to bad hams before curtain goes up

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Playwright giving way to bad hams before curtain goes up (3,7)': anagram of HAMS (4) plus reversed DRAPE gives 9 letters; one S is unaccounted for ('shams' would fit) and no source found to confirm the printed text.
annotationWithheld.clue: Playwright giving way to bad hams before curtain goes up

clue.text: Creature from outer space found on a lump of metal

indicators.note: the outer letters of space are its first and last

parts.note: a slug is a lump of metal, such as a bullet

explanation.surface: An alien creature discovered resting on a chunk of metal.
explanation.definitionFit: This marine mollusc without a shell is a living creature.

clue.text: Novel source of energy — gas!

indicators.note: the letters of the words are the raw source from which the title is made

explanation.surface: Excited praise of gas as a new kind of energy supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' reads as 'new', but it names a book; ENERGY and GAS rearranged give the title.
explanation.definitionFit: This is Anne Brontë's first published book, so it is a novel.

clue.text: City gent given coat and hat by principal?

parts.note: Frank stands for any man's name, a gent
a fur is a coat
a tam is a Scottish cap
main means principal, chief

explanation.surface: A City gentleman being dressed by his chief.
explanation.definitionFit: The German financial centre on the River Main is a city.

clue.text: This may be put on legal documents, we hear

indicators.note: signals that the clue's word is said aloud

parts.note: writs are formal legal documents

explanation.surface: Something that might be stamped on official legal papers.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the idiom 'put on the Ritz', to show off grandly.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'put on the Ritz' means to dress up or display luxury, referring to the grand hotel.

clue.text: After massage, shampoo left in navel?

indicators.note: massaging works the letters into a new shape

explanation.surface: Shampoo residue left in the belly button after a massage.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek word for navel, also used for a central point.

clue.text: Hair treatment in Torquay area given to sound swimmer

indicators.note: the hair treatment sits inside the area letters

parts.note: Torquay is a Devon resort in south-west England, abbreviated SW
a perm is a curling hair treatment
sound means healthy, hale

explanation.surface: A hairdo in a Devon seaside town given to a healthy swimmer.
explanation.definitionFit: The great toothed whale is a large ocean swimmer.

clue.text: We declare Charlie Parker to be a noted homemaker

parts.note: to aver is to declare
Bird was the nickname of jazz saxophonist Charlie Parker

explanation.surface: Announcing that the jazz saxophonist was famously domestic.
explanation.definitionFit: This African bird is famous for weaving elaborate nests, a skilled home builder.

clue.text: Bra may be smaller with bits going round in front

indicators.note: the turned piece stands ahead of the word for smaller
turning round means reading the word for bits backwards

parts.note: parts are bits
less means smaller

explanation.surface: A bra might be reduced by having pieces wrapping round the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bra may be' is a definition by example, an adjective a bra can carry; 'going round' turns the word for bits back to front, and 'in front' puts it ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: A bra without shoulder straps is described by this adjective.

clue.text: Coolness needed if dragons are to be overcome?

indicators.note: overcome dragons are knocked about, so their letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Asking whether calm is required to defeat dragons.
explanation.definitionFit: French for 'cold blood', it means composure under pressure.

clue.text: Portable device providing about 50% more space

indicators.note: about signals that the pieces are turned back to front
half of the word more, here its latter two letters

parts.note: a gap is a space

explanation.surface: A gadget that offers half as much room again.
explanation.walkthrough: '50%' takes RE from 'more'; 'about' turns REGAP round.
explanation.definitionFit: A beeper is a small device carried around for receiving messages.

clue.text: Introduction of naval vessel that's more up-to-date

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: a ewer is a jug, a vessel

explanation.surface: The launch of a modern warship.
explanation.definitionFit: A comparative meaning more recent, more modern.

clue.text: C-in-C on Rocket?

parts.note: a commander-in-chief is the head of war, and the explosive top of a missile sits on a rocket

explanation.definitionFit: The explosive tip of a missile, punningly a war chief.

clue.text: Air marshal — on his belly?

parts.note: a vent lets out air
to rally is to marshal or gather troops

explanation.surface: An RAF air marshal lying face down.
explanation.definitionFit: Ventral refers to the belly side, so the adverb means positioned on the underside.

clue.text: The girl messing about in a boat

indicators.note: messing about jumbles the letters

explanation.surface: A girl idling in a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat-bottomed barge used to unload ships is a boat.

clue.text: Stoking boiler for Rocket?

definitions.meaning: tending the fire is a stoker's job, labour at the furnace
a rocket is one kind of pyrotechnic display item

explanation.definitionFit: Feeding a furnace is literally labour with fire, and a rocket is an example of a pyrotechnic.

clue.text: Interjection that's archaic, say, in the current era

parts.note: eg, for example, means say
AD is the abbreviation for the Christian era

explanation.surface: An old exclamation still used in modern times.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned mild oath meaning 'by God'.

clue.text: A film director plunged two metres into a river

indicators.note: the metres go into the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, Cheshire and Scotland
M is the abbreviation for metre, twice

explanation.surface: A movie director diving two metres into a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Jonathan Demme directed The Silence of the Lambs.

clue.text: Only odd anglers read The Times

indicators.note: only the odd-numbered letters of the word are kept

explanation.surface: Only eccentric fishermen read a certain newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Ages are eras or periods of history, times.

clue.text: Literal contents of empty pockets

indicators.note: the contents of the phrase are letters lying within it

explanation.surface: The things found in empty pockets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Literal' is a printer's term for a misprint.
explanation.definitionFit: A literal is printers' jargon for a misprinted letter.

clue.text: Windows possibly get obscured or panes get misty

indicators.note: obscured letters are clouded and mixed up

explanation.surface: Panes of glass becoming hidden or clouding up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Windows' looks like glass panes, but it is Microsoft's software.
explanation.definitionFit: Microsoft Windows is an example of the software that runs a computer.

clue.text: A western city to avoid

definitions.meaning: a Kansas town of Wild West fame

explanation.definitionFit: Dodge City in Kansas was a Wild West town, and the verb means evade.

clue.text: Talk shows do cruises at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: Talks are held on shows aboard cruise ships.
explanation.definitionFit: A discourse is a formal talk or spoken discussion.
